# Luminous

> Luminous is a free, open-source, native desktop music player for the audio library you already own — local-first, no streaming, no subscriptions, no cloud. Currently at version 3.2, available in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Russian, and Ukrainian.

## What's New in 3.2
- Missing drive protection: when a large share of a folder's songs vanish at once (an unplugged external drive or a renamed folder), Luminous keeps them in your library and asks before removing anything
- Stutter-free remote streaming on WebDAV and Subsonic, with read-ahead buffering, pooled connections, and faster track starts
- Sharper artist portraits out of the box: a built-in fanart.tv key, with Deezer and Wikidata fallbacks
- Lyrics source badge showing where the current lyrics came from: embedded tags, a sidecar file, an online provider, your own edits, or the local cache
- No startup freeze on very large libraries, plus AppImage delta updates via .zsync on Linux

## What's New in 3.1
- ASIO output on Windows: stream directly to external DACs and audio interfaces through a pure-Rust ASIO backend, with native sample rate switching
- Audio device and backend selection in Settings → System (shared system audio or Direct Hardware ASIO), with access to the driver's own control panel; output recovers automatically when devices are plugged in or removed
- Song and Artist Radio: right-click any song or artist and choose Start Song Radio or Start Artist Radio for a 25-song queue built entirely from your local library's metadata and play history — no cloud services
- Faster startup and smoother Albums grid scrolling on large libraries, plus many stability fixes

## What's New in 3.0
- Seven languages: German, Spanish, Italian, Russian, and Ukrainian join English and French, with regional English (US, UK) and French (France) variants, a translated user guide, and the bundled Fira Sans font (including Cyrillic)
- Love and rate: love a song (or dislike it with a right-click on the heart) and give it 1–5 stars independently; sign in with MusicBrainz to sync loves and ratings with ListenBrainz and CritiqueBrainz
- Parametric EQ: up to 20 free-frequency bell or shelf bands you drag on the response graph or type exactly, AutoEq headphone profile import, and presets with response-curve previews
- Lyrics: live lyrics in the miniplayer, word-by-word sync, timing offset, right-to-left text, and .srt/.vtt sidecar files
- Info sidebar: the right panel follows what you're viewing — the selected song, album, or artist — and can be unpinned into a hover overlay
- Pinned playlists, albums, and artists in the sidebar, grids instead of carousels, and a Cards/Rows toggle
- Auto-organize: new files and tag changes are moved into your folder pattern as they arrive
- Portable mode with a standalone Windows ZIP; library folders re-link when a drive letter changes
- Much faster first and repeat WebDAV syncs for large libraries, with a report of files that failed to sync
- fanart.tv logos, backgrounds, and disc art; opt-in sidecar artwork; upcoming concerts on artist pages
- Auto Continue keeps playing similar music when the queue runs out
- Online/Offline toggle that turns off every online source and service
- Supporter add-on themes from the Microsoft Store, and setting Luminous as the default player on Windows
- AppImage is back for Linux

## What's New in 2.5
- OpenSubsonic streaming: connect Navidrome, Nextcloud Music, Gonic, LMS, or any Subsonic-compatible server and sync its library into Luminous
- Two-way server sync: plays, favourites, and ratings sync back to the server
- Artist enrichment: MusicBrainz artist details, with portraits from fanart.tv and Wikidata
- Album links to Discogs, AllMusic, Wikidata, and lyrics providers
- Audio Pipeline inspector: decode format, sample rate, bit depth, gain, and output device, plus a playbar quality badge
- Opus playback
- Repeat Album mode
- Smart playlists from folders
- Share cards for playlists, artists, and personal stats
- Official Flatpak from a self-hosted, auto-updating repo

## What's New in 2.0
- Listening Stats: streaks, top artists and albums, and time-of-day listening patterns
- Redesigned Organize Files: clearer preview and destination flow when renaming and sorting your library
- Pin to Home: pin favorite artists, albums, and playlists to the Home screen
- Moment Mix: an auto-generated playlist that shifts with the time of day
- MusicBrainz Picard integration: hand off tag lookups to Picard from the tag editor
- WebDAV support: connect a WebDAV server and add its music into your library
- Artist & Album Artwork: local-artwork scanner finds artist portraits, band logos, and fanart on disk
- Social Share Cards: share what you're listening to with generated social images
- Bios & Links: add markdown bios and links to artists and albums
- Discord & ListenBrainz: share live listening as a Discord presence and scrobble to ListenBrainz

## Core Features
- Local audio library indexing with instant search across artists, albums, and songs
- Gapless playback for MP3, FLAC, Opus, WAV, and other formats
- Remote sources: OpenSubsonic servers and WebDAV
- Artist pages filled in automatically from MusicBrainz and fanart.tv: logos, artwork, bio, links, and upcoming concerts
- Info sidebar with details for the song, album, or artist you're viewing
- Smart and auto playlists (built around decades, genres, and BPM)
- Custom genre hierarchies via drag-and-drop sub-genre organization
- Love and 1–5 star ratings, synced with ListenBrainz when signed in with MusicBrainz
- Song and Artist Radio: instant queues built from your local library
- Compact, always-on-top miniplayer with live lyrics
- Predefined and dynamic (cover-art-driven) themes
- Time-synced lyrics, line by line or word by word, with inline editing
- Advanced `field:value` search syntax (e.g. `genre:rock`), savable as smart playlists
- Built-in tag editor for single or bulk metadata edits, with MusicBrainz Picard handoff
- ASIO output on Windows for external DACs and audio interfaces
- 10-band graphic EQ with genre presets, plus a 20-band free-frequency parametric EQ with AutoEq headphone profiles
- File organization into folders from your own naming template, automatically as new music arrives
- Listening stats: streaks, top artists and albums, and time-of-day patterns
- Portable mode for running from a USB drive
- Available in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Russian, and Ukrainian

## Tech Stack & Architecture
- Framework: Tauri v2 (native — no Electron)
- Frontend: SvelteKit (Svelte 5) / TypeScript / Tailwind CSS
- Core Backend: Rust
- Lightweight, no subscriptions, no data collection
